- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 10–15 days).
- Forecast shows gradual upward bias (slight overcorrection) after initial underestimation, suggesting lagged response to recent price spikes.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), model fails to capture subsequent sharp drops or mean reversion, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model exhibits diminishing sensitivity to recent history as forecast horizon extends — later days show less adjustment to true values.
- Forecast tends to plateau or slightly rise after initial correction, missing abrupt downward corrections in true outcomes.
- Model underestimates true values when recent history includes strong downward trends (e.g., 75–80 range), failing to anticipate further decline.
- Forecast often overcorrects after a spike, leading to overshoot in mid-forecast period (e.g., 80.5–81.5 range) before true price drops below 78.
- Model does not adequately adjust for mean reversion in the 75–80 range — consistently underestimates true values when prices are near or below 78.
- Forecast shows weak reaction to true price volatility — fails to capture sudden drops or spikes in the last 5–7 days of the horizon.
